Definition: of immediate Latin origin, but ultimately a derivative of G138 in the sense of its cognate G1507; a coil (spira, "spire"), i.e. (figuratively) a mass of men (a Roman military cohort; also (by analogy) a squad of Levitical janitors):--band.
BiblicalUsage: A band is a Roman cohort, six hundred men under one command. Cornelius is a centurion of the band called the Italian band, and Judas comes to the garden having received a band of men and officers, and the band and the captain take Jesus and bind Him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the bands show the two powers at work in Acts: Rome's soldiers and the Lord's church, and the cohort that arrested Jesus could not hold Him.
